note: Module checks and final check for the Level 3 Mould Remediation draft (GP-658). Original CARSI questions; no standard text. SME review required before seeding.

questions.questionText: What sets the remediation method on a mould job?
questions.explanation: The method follows the Condition of each area and how far hidden growth may reach. Area is a warning sign that the job needs Level 3 planning, not the thing that sets the method.

questions.questionText: A 6 m² job is in an aged care home. Is it Level 3?
questions.explanation: One trigger is enough. Vulnerable occupants make even a small job a Level 3 job, because the planning and controls step up, and so does coordination.

questions.questionText: Visible growth of 14.4 m², 7.8 m² and 9.6 m² is found on two floors. What is the total?
questions.explanation: 14.4 + 7.8 + 9.6 = 31.8 m². That is more than three times the Level 2 band before any wall is opened.

questions.questionText: In Geelong the ducted air-conditioning still runs. What is the first decision?
questions.explanation: A running system can carry spores to every room it serves. Switch it off and isolate it before scoping further.

questions.questionText: Several businesses share a duty on one site. What must each one do?
questions.explanation: Under section 46 of the model WHS Act, each duty holder must, so far as is reasonably practicable, consult with the others, and cooperate and coordinate with them.

questions.questionText: Does consulting the builder move your duty for your crew's work to them?
questions.explanation: Consulting and coordinating does not transfer a duty. Your company still owns the risks of its own work.

questions.questionText: From what cost of construction work does a project need a principal contractor?
questions.explanation: Under the model WHS Regulations a construction project is construction work costing $250,000 or more. It has a principal contractor, who prepares a WHS management plan.

questions.questionText: What does the remediation work plan set out that the SWMS does not?
questions.explanation: The work plan sets out what will be done, in work order. The SWMS sets out how the high risk construction work is done safely.

questions.questionText: Scaffold work has its deck at 4.6 m. Is it high risk construction work?
options: No, scaffold work is always safe
Only when powered plant is used
questions.explanation: Work with a risk of a person falling more than 2 metres is high risk construction work, so a SWMS must be prepared before it starts.

questions.questionText: The crew is not following the SWMS. What must happen?
questions.explanation: Work must be done in line with the SWMS. If it is not, it is stopped immediately or as soon as it is safe, and does not restart until it is.

questions.questionText: A technician's fit test is 14 months old. Can they enter in that respirator?
questions.explanation: Safe Work Australia guidance is to fit test at least once a year and with each new make or model. An out-of-date fit test means no entry in that respirator.

questions.questionText: A worker in a coverall becomes confused near shift end. What do you do?
questions.explanation: Confusion in the heat is a medical emergency. Call 000, get them out of the work area at once, cool them and give first aid.

questions.questionText: With 45-minute work periods each hour, how much hands-on work is in a 10-hour shift?
questions.explanation: 10 × 45 minutes = 450 minutes = 7.5 hours. Plan the job duration on hands-on time, not shift length.

questions.questionText: Which record shows who was inside a zone, and for how long?
questions.explanation: An entry and exit log for each zone records who went in, when, when they came out and the respirator worn. It also shows who has been in the heat longest.

questions.questionText: Why confirm a thermal-camera suspect with a moisture meter?
questions.explanation: A thermal camera shows temperature. A cool patch can be a draught or missing insulation, so confirm each suspect with a meter.

questions.questionText: What goes in place before drilling a 25 mm inspection hole into a cavity?
questions.explanation: Opening up for inspection should use source control: a HEPA nozzle at the cut and a small film barrier. Full containment comes before full opening.

questions.questionText: A bearer under the wall may be rotten. Who decides what happens to it?
questions.explanation: Load-bearing members go to a structural engineer. You record what you saw; the engineer decides what it means and what support is needed.

questions.questionText: Twenty 25 mm holes replace opening 28.8 m² of wall. What do they give you?
questions.explanation: Small controlled openings show which bays are affected, so the containment and removal are sized on evidence rather than guesswork.

questions.questionText: Air has a dew point of 14.4 °C. A ceiling corner is 12.5 °C. What happens?
questions.explanation: The surface is below the dew point of the room air, so water condenses on it. Repeated nightly, that feeds mould.

questions.questionText: A ten-year-old exhaust fan discharges into the roof space. How do you report it?
questions.explanation: Write what you observed, against the NCC benchmark. Compliance and defect findings belong to building surveyors and certifiers, or tribunals.

questions.questionText: Why log indoor and outdoor conditions over several days?
questions.explanation: Condensation depends on cold nights and moisture load, which change day to day. A single reading can miss the pattern.

questions.questionText: Is the 10 m² asbestos threshold permission for a mould crew to remove asbestos?
options: No, it is a licensing rule
Yes, if it is wetted down
Yes, if the crew wear P2
questions.explanation: The 10 m² figure decides when a removal licence is needed. It is not permission for a mould crew to remove asbestos; refer it.

questions.questionText: Asbestos-cement eaves of 11.7 m² must come out. Who removes them?
questions.explanation: More than 10 m² of non-friable asbestos needs a Class B (or Class A) licensed removalist, then a clearance certificate.

questions.questionText: Paint tests at 2.3% lead. What changes before anyone machine sands it?
questions.explanation: Machine sanding paint with more than 1% lead by dry weight is a lead process under the model WHS Regulations. Plan lead controls or avoid sanding.

questions.questionText: On a sewage job, why start drying only after soaked porous materials are out?
questions.explanation: Air movers blowing across contaminated material spread it. Remove soaked porous materials and clean first, then dry.

questions.questionText: What does the Immunisation Handbook recommend for sewage workers?
questions.explanation: The Australian Immunisation Handbook recommends hepatitis A vaccine for plumbers and sewage workers.

questions.questionText: Plasterboard comes out to 1.8 m on 96 m of wall, both faces. About how much?
questions.explanation: 96 × 1.8 = 172.8 m² per face. Both faces = 345.6 m².

questions.questionText: Who must give written consent before contents from a flooded building are thrown out?
questions.explanation: Contents decisions need the owner's written consent before disposal, with an inventory of each item and its condition.

questions.questionText: Why split a large loss into zones?
questions.explanation: Zones can each be sealed and checked on their own. A breach affects one zone, and finished areas stay clean.

questions.questionText: A 181.4 m³ zone needs 6 air changes per hour. Each scrubber gives 500 m³/h. How many?
Who arranges the isolation of a smoke detector in a zone?
questions.explanation: Detectors and sprinklers are part of the building's fire safety system. The building manager's agreement is not enough: the fire services contractor isolates them under a written impairment plan, and the system is restored and tested before you leave each day.

questions.questionText: Where does a two-stage decontamination chamber help most?
questions.explanation: A dirty room and a clean room keep heavy dust and spores out of clean areas when large amounts of material are being removed.

questions.questionText: What minimum pressure difference does S520 recommend for a containment?
questions.explanation: S520 section 9.3.3 recommends a minimum of −5 Pa. Confirm the figure against AS-IICRC S520:2025.

questions.questionText: Where does a zone manometer's reference tube go?
questions.explanation: The reference sits in the clean area the zone protects, so the reading shows whether air flows from clean to dirty.

questions.questionText: Eight readings at 5-minute intervals are above the limit. How long was it out?
questions.explanation: 8 × 5 = 40 minutes. Record the event, the cause, the fix and who you told.

questions.questionText: A zone alarm trips. What comes first?
questions.explanation: Stop work in the zone, find the cause and fix it, wait for recovery, then record and report the event.

questions.questionText: Why must the HVAC stay off while the work area is contaminated?
questions.explanation: A running system carries spores to every room it serves and can draw contamination into the ducts.

questions.questionText: Porous-lined flexible duct is spotted with growth inside. Clean or replace?
questions.explanation: Flexible and internally lined ducts have porous linings. Growth in them usually means replacement.

questions.questionText: A 600 mm × 400 mm duct is 18 m long. What is its internal surface area?
Who connects a temporary board to a three-phase switchboard?
questions.explanation: Connecting temporary supply or a generator is electrical installation work and must be done by a licensed electrician.

questions.questionText: 14 × 6.5 A, 8 × 4.5 A and 20 × 1.2 A. What is the total current?
questions.explanation: 91 + 36 + 24 = 151 A, about 50 A per phase when balanced.

questions.questionText: Why stagger switching on 14 compressor dehumidifiers?
questions.explanation: Compressor dehumidifiers draw more current for a moment when they start. Starting them together can trip the supply.

questions.questionText: Why does dust matter more in an aged care home than an empty office?
questions.explanation: People with weakened immune systems can develop serious fungal infections, such as aspergillosis, from airborne spores.

questions.questionText: Who do you plan healthcare work with before starting?
questions.explanation: The national healthcare infection control guidelines expect infection prevention and control staff on the team for construction and renovation work.

questions.questionText: 208.7 m³ at 8 air changes per hour. How much air is needed?
questions.explanation: 208.7 × 8 = 1,670 m³/h, so four scrubbers at 500 m³/h real airflow, plus a spare.

questions.questionText: Residents in a memory support wing may try to enter. What control helps most?
questions.explanation: Residents may not understand signs. Use a physical barrier they cannot open and supervise the entry.

questions.questionText: Who tells families about the work and any health questions?
questions.explanation: Give the service the facts in writing and let it communicate. Do not discuss health risks with parents yourself.

questions.questionText: What is the strongest control in a childcare centre or school?
questions.explanation: The safest children are the ones not in the building. Time dusty work for holidays, weekends or closure days.

questions.questionText: A 14-day closure needs 13 days of work. What do you agree in advance?
options: What happens if it runs late
A higher price for more speed
Skipping the verification step if late
Removing the drying goal from scope
questions.explanation: With no buffer, agree in writing what happens if results are late, for example the rooms stay closed, not the centre.

questions.questionText: Who maintains and repairs common property in a strata scheme?
questions.explanation: Strata laws, such as section 106 of the NSW Act, make the owners corporation responsible for common property.

questions.questionText: Do you decide whether a waterproofing membrane is common property?
questions.explanation: Boundaries depend on the strata plan and the state's rules. The strata manager confirms them; you report the facts.

questions.questionText: Why report areas of 6.3 m², 8.3 m² and 27.0 m² separately by location?
questions.explanation: Reporting by lot and common area lets the owners corporation, the owners and the insurer see the scope in each part of the building.

questions.questionText: Work must happen while children are present. Which set-up is right?
questions.explanation: With children present the work area must be completely separate: its own outside entry, solid barriers, negative pressure and no shared air-conditioning.

questions.questionText: A shared riser in a strata building has growth inside. What kind of issue is it?
questions.explanation: A shared riser serves several units. Growth in it is a common property matter that affects every unit it serves.

quizzes.title: Level 3 Mould Remediation — Final check: Level 3 Mould Remediation

questions.questionText: Which single trigger makes a 6 m² job Level 3?
questions.explanation: Vulnerable occupants are a Level 3 trigger on their own, whatever the area.

questions.questionText: Under the model WHS Act, which section requires duty holders to consult, cooperate and coordinate?
questions.explanation: Section 46 covers the duty to consult with other duty holders. Section 19 is the primary duty of care.

questions.questionText: When must a SWMS for high risk construction work be prepared?
questions.explanation: Under the model WHS Regulations a SWMS must be prepared before high risk construction work starts.

questions.questionText: What should you use to confirm a cool patch on a thermal image?
questions.explanation: A thermal camera shows temperature, not water. Confirm every suspect with a moisture meter.

questions.questionText: Which date does Queensland use for buildings in its asbestos rules?
questions.explanation: The model laws use 31 December 2003, but Queensland's regulation uses 31 December 1989 for buildings (31 December 2003 for other structures and plant). Whatever the date, test before cutting if unsure.

questions.questionText: What must be issued before an asbestos removal area is reoccupied?
questions.explanation: After licensed removal, an independent person inspects and issues a clearance certificate before the area is reoccupied.

questions.questionText: What is the safe order on a sewage-affected mould job?
questions.explanation: Remove soaked porous materials, then clean and sanitise, then dry. Drying first spreads contamination.

questions.questionText: What does S520 section 9.3.5 give as the minimum air changes per hour?
questions.explanation: Section 9.3.5 gives at least 4 air changes per hour. Confirm against AS-IICRC S520:2025.

questions.questionText: What should a data-logging manometer do when a zone loses pressure?
questions.explanation: Set the logger to alarm when the reading rises above the plan limit, and test the alarm on day one.

questions.questionText: Which Australian standards series covers microbial control in building air-handling systems?
questions.explanation: AS/NZS 3666 covers microbial control of air-handling and water systems. AS/NZS 3012 is construction site electrics.

questions.questionText: Who may work on the refrigerant circuit of an air-conditioning unit?
options: A technician with an ARC refrigerant handling licence
questions.explanation: Work that could release fluorocarbon refrigerant needs an ARC refrigerant handling licence. Cleaning coils, ducts or filters doesn't, but the refrigerant circuit is for a licensed technician.

questions.questionText: Where must a generator run on a large job?
questions.explanation: Engines produce carbon monoxide. Run generators outdoors with the exhaust away from any opening.

questions.questionText: In a healthcare facility, who decides with the verification when an area is reoccupied?
questions.explanation: The facility's infection prevention and control lead decides reoccupation together with the independent verification.

questions.questionText: In strata, who confirms common property boundaries?
options: The strata manager, from the plan
The remediator, from the site inspection
The tenant, from the lease terms
The insurer, from the claim form
questions.explanation: Boundaries come from the strata plan and the state's rules. The strata manager confirms them.

questions.questionText: Why should clearance be confirmed by a party independent of the remediator?
questions.explanation: The company that did the work has an interest in it passing. Independent verification is what others can rely on.

questions.questionText: A spore trap sampled 0.075 m³ and counted 96 spores. What is the concentration?
questions.explanation: 96 ÷ 0.075 = 1,280 spores per cubic metre.

questions.questionText: How is an indoor air result usually interpreted?
questions.explanation: There is no numerical health-based limit for airborne mould, so hygienists compare indoor with outdoor and affected with unaffected areas.

questions.questionText: You find growth beyond the agreed scope. What comes before carrying on?
questions.explanation: Make safe and record it, notify, then agree the change in writing before working on the new scope.

questions.questionText: A claim is declined or not paid in full. How fast must relied-on expert reports be given?
questions.explanation: Paragraphs 81–82 of the General Insurance Code of Practice give 10 business days when a claim is declined or not paid in full. Write every report expecting the owner to read it.

questions.questionText: Which belongs in your remediation report?
questions.explanation: Report the likely cause and the evidence. Liability and cover, like health, are for others to decide.

questions.questionText: Which sample shows whether growth is inside a piece of plasterboard?
questions.explanation: A bulk sample is a piece of the material itself, so the lab can see whether growth is inside it. Air and dust samples show what is in the air or has settled.
